To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the delay-interval stimuli used in this study had differential effects on the accuracy of delayed matching to sample in pigeons and (b) the delay-intervall stimuli had differential effects on ongoing operant key pecking.

(a) illumination of the houselights and the center key, with white geometric forms, decreased matching performance, (b) presentation of a tone or vibration of the chamber did not decrease matching performance, and (c) illumination of the test chamber with a white geometric form or the houselights decreased pecking rate.
stimuli that interfere with delayed matching to sample also interfere with simple operant responding, and that the interference is greater with delay-interval stimuli that are more complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of stimuli presented during the delay period on performance in a delayed matching-to-sample task.
the effects of delay-interval events on the performance of pigeons in delayed matching to sample.
the effects of various stimuli on the performance of pigeons in delayed matching to sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of the delay interval stimuli are not due to their effects on the delay interval per se but to their effects on other processes.

the results of the present study are consistent with the notion of a limited capacity system that can be overloaded, and with the notion that the system is sensitive to a variety of stimuli. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved)

the results of Experiment 1 are consistent with the hypothesis that memory for the presence of a sample is a necessary condition for the occurrence of delayed matching to sample behavior, whereas the results of Experiment II are consistent with the notion that the delay-interval stimuli interfere with the memory trace for the presence of the sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of delay interval stimuli on matching accuracy and key pecking are similar, and that the effects of these stimuli on matching performance are mediated by their effects on the ongoing operant behavior.
the stimuli which interfere with memory also interfere with other forms of behavior.

the effects of delay interval stimulation on matching performance are not due to the delay interval stimuli themselves, but rather to the fact that these stimuli are novel and thus disrupt ongoing behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stimuli used to test memory are important.
the effects of delay interval stimuli on matching accuracy are not due to the delay interval stimuli being remembered.
the delay stimuli we used in our study had the effect of making the birds less attentive to the task, and this was true whether or not the stimuli were presented during training.
